title: 2001 HMMT February Calculus Problem 7
statement: Find the coefficient of \(x^{12}\) in the Maclaurin series (i.e. Taylor series around \(x=0\) ) for \(\frac{1}{1-3 x+2 x^{2}}\).

solutions.text: If you know formal power series, then this is not such a hard question, but since this is a calculus test... Use partial fractions to get \(\frac{1}{1-3 x+2 x^{2}}=\frac{1 / 2}{1-2 x}-\frac{1}{1-x}\). Now each of these can be expanded as a geometric series (or take derivatives and get the same result) to get \(\frac{1}{2}\left(1+2 x+4 x^{2}+8 x^{3}+\cdots\right)-\left(1+x+x^{2}+x^{3}+\cdots\right)\), so the coefficient of \(x^{n}\) is \(2^{n-1}-1\). When \(n=12\), that's 2047 .
